title: [Spec Decode] Lazily catch up draft KV after zero-K steps (#734)
quote: record the earliest missing draft-KV position during K=0 without running the draft model, then lazily ingest the complete missing range before the next K>0 proposal
proves: Merged 2026-09-15 (by LxYuan0420, author POWEHI2023). Implements lazy draft-KV catch-up after K=0 steps; lazy path only with prefix caching off ("enable_prefix_caching=True keeps the eager" path); median wall 0.8610 s eager vs 0.7754 s lazy, -9.94%, on Qwen3-0.6B dynamic K, three alternating pairs; proposal hashes, target outputs and acceptance counts identical across six processes (18/18 accepted).
does_not_prove: REVIEWER CLAIM NOT SUPPORTED (in part): "exact acceptance" is only an observed equality on one small benchmark (18 proposed tokens), not a stated guarantee or a general test. PR says the speedup is specific to this workload. Other reviewer details (merge date, prefix-caching exclusion, -9.94%) are supported.
bearing: C3' prior art: lazy catch-up already shipped in vllm-metal; weakens novelty, leaves prefix-caching case open

title: Utility-Driven Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts (Cascade)
venue: The 58th IEEE/ACM International Symposium on Microarchitecture, Seoul, Oct 18-22 2025
quote: We present, Cascade, a utility-driven speculation framework to dynamically disable speculation if it is detrimental.
proves: Cascade disables speculation when not useful and keeps state consistent by executing the drafter even when speculation is off, at "a modest overhead of 2-3% on average"; targets model-based drafters like EAGLE (n-gram has no KV state).
does_not_prove: REVIEWER CLAIM NOT SUPPORTED (in part): the paper does not call the 2-3% a synchronization cost; it is the cost of running the drafter while speculation is off (eager catch-up). Page names the venue in full, not the label "MICRO 2025". Does not study lazy catch-up.
bearing: C3': eager baseline (always run drafter) with stated cost; supports lazy catch-up as an improvement target

title: [Feature] Batch-invariant support for speculative decoding (#52522)
quote: This PR extends batch invariance to stochastic speculative decoding.
proves: Open PR (merge conflicts). On preemption recovery it caps the prefix-cache hit at L-2 tokens, replays the token to rebuild the target hidden state and regenerates the proposal from that boundary; E2E test test_spec_batch_invariance_with_preemption uses small KV and asserts preemption occurred before comparing serial vs batched token IDs. Validated EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark; MTP untested.
does_not_prove: Not merged; page does not show the test passing in CI; earlier GSM8K run had zero preemptions. Covers preemption, not K=0 resume.
bearing: C7': exact-output oracle under preemption already proposed upstream; threatens novelty of C7' for preemption

title: [RFC]: Batch invariance for speculative decoding needs to cover the forward pass (M=1 vs M=k+1) (#54506)
quote: draft acceptance ~100% → 72% and decode ~110 → 89 tok/s
proves: Open RFC (opened 2026-08-31) arguing forward-pass batch invariance across M for a fixed logical row should be "a first-class contract"; reports acceptance ~100% to 72% and decode ~110 to 89 tok/s on one workload.
does_not_prove: REVIEWER CLAIM NOT SUPPORTED (in part): the page does not establish that invariance "must" cover M=1 vs M=k+1; it asks maintainers whether this is a guarantee or explicit non-guarantee. Numbers are from a single workload.
bearing: C7': shows exact acceptance equivalence is not currently guaranteed; oracle needs M-invariant kernels

title: [Bug][Spec Decode] MRV2 AutoRegressiveSpeculator ignores dynamic K from scheduler - DSD non-functional on MRV2 (#51510)
quote: ignores the scheduler's per-step dynamic K selection
proves: Open issue: with VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 the speculator ignores per-step dynamic K and "always runs the full static-K draft pipeline".
does_not_prove: Does not say how K=0 state is handled once fixed; open, no fix shown.
bearing: C3': on MRV2 the K=0 catch-up question does not arise yet; a bug class the oracle could catch

title: Dynamic Speculative Decoding (vLLM docs, stable)
quote: Not compatible with data parallelism ( `--data-parallel-size > 1`).
proves: DSD tested with Eagle, Eagle-3, DFlash; incompatible with DP because ranks pick different K; falls back to static K. K=0 is supported: "K=0 will be used when the concurrency is in range [129, 512]".
does_not_prove: Does not describe how draft state is caught up after K=0 steps.
bearing: C3': K=0 is an official upstream mode, so catch-up after K=0 is a real path

title: Adaptive Speculative Decoding (SGLang docs)
quote: Must be a non-empty list of positive ints; a slot that omits it raises a config error.
proves: candidate_steps must be positive integers, so a zero step tier is not configurable.
does_not_prove: Page never states "no K=0" explicitly; this is an inference from "positive ints". Does not cover other SGLang paths that turn speculation off.
bearing: C3': SGLang adaptive mode avoids K=0, narrowing C3' to vLLM/vllm-metal

title: Finding Crash-Consistency Bugs with Bounded Black-Box Crash Testing
quote: We present a new approach to testing file-system crash consistency: bounded black-box crash testing (B3).
proves: B3 approach with tools CrashMonkey and Ace; found 24 of 26 crash-consistency bugs reported in the prior five years.
does_not_prove: File systems only; says nothing about LLM serving or speculative decoding.
bearing: C7' method precedent: bounded enumeration of workloads plus an oracle

title: [Bugfix] Carry a resumed request's whole sequence in the prefill pack (#892)
quote: the draft-model catch-up derived a negative chunk offset
proves: Merged 2026-09-29. _build_prefill_pack cut tokens at prompt_len, so a request resumed after preemption reached the pack with only its prompt; draft-model catch-up derived a negative chunk offset (also broke penalties/min_tokens and M-RoPE). Fix carries state.token_ids whole.
does_not_prove: Resume after preemption, not resume after K=0; does not say the bug was caught by an acceptance-equivalence oracle.
bearing: C3'/C7': real catch-up bug on resume in vllm-metal; evidence the bug class exists

title: [Test] Audit complete DFlash and DSpark serving continuations (#1035)
quote: The serving parity tool can report `TOP_K_MATCH` after checking only the first divergent token.
proves: Merged 2026-10-06. Adds opt-in --audit-continuations that replays every emitted token through native mlx-lm; strict runs exit 1 because native greedy equivalence is incomplete even for target-only serving; 15-21 argmax mismatches per 1,280 DSpark tokens on Qwen3-4B/8B.
does_not_prove: REVIEWER CLAIM NOT SUPPORTED: "continuations" means the full emitted output sequence, not resume/preemption/catch-up; the PR does not audit serving continuations in that sense. It "does not change serving math or establish a speedup".
bearing: C7' threat: vllm-metal is not even greedy-exact vs native mlx-lm, so an exact oracle needs a self-consistent baseline

title: Roadmap (#1005)
quote: validate state rollback, rejection, prefix reuse, preemption, and recomputation.
proves: Open pinned roadmap; under speculative decoding, for native hybrid GDN MTP with prefix caching, lists validating state rollback, rejection, prefix reuse, preemption and recomputation (tracking #610).
does_not_prove: Scoped to hybrid GDN MTP, not draft-model K=0 catch-up; a plan, not a result.
bearing: C7': maintainers want this validation; supports demand

title: DSpark in SGLang: Speculative Decoding with Confidence-Driven, Variable-Length Verification
quote: Trimming censors the ceiling: compact mode only verifies a block's first few positions
proves: Compact mode verifies only the first positions, so full-block acceptance at that step is never observed; cap-accept mode recovers the ceiling.
does_not_prove: Not about catch-up or correctness oracles.
bearing: C7' caveat: acceptance metrics under trimming are censored, so equivalence must compare like modes

title: TensorSharp2 speculative decoding doc
quote: n-gram mines the emitted token history, which is complete whatever the KV cache did
proves: n-gram drafter history comes from emitted tokens; SeedCommitted seeds it on a reused prefix (else "an EMPTY corpus" and it stays silent); SpeculativeExecution.CatchUp commits tokens generated plainly in a mixed phase "with no hidden rows".
does_not_prove: REVIEWER CLAIM NOT SUPPORTED (in part): no explicit "rebuild suffix history" procedure; the drafter is n-gram, not suffix-tree, and the mechanism is seeding/catch-up commits. Year not shown.
bearing: C3': another engine with explicit drafter catch-up after a plain phase

title: tensorrt_llm/_torch/speculative/interface.py
quote: can attach draft KV an unchunked prefill would not produce. Acceptance only.
proves: Code comment: for vanilla MTP, an internal chunk lacks target_hidden[i + k], so reuse can attach draft KV that an unchunked prefill would not produce, affecting acceptance only. An env var forces accepted tokens with fractional rates (e.g. 2.6) "for testing and debugging speculative decoding."
does_not_prove: Only first 100k of 159k chars read. Does not quantify the acceptance loss.
bearing: C7': chunking changes draft KV, so acceptance equivalence is not exact across chunk boundaries in TRT-LLM; forced acceptance is a testing knob

title: Attention Drift: What Autoregressive Speculative Decoding Models Learn
quote: attention progressively moves from the prompt onto its own recently-generated tokens
proves: Within a speculation chain the drafter's attention moves from the prompt to its own recently generated tokens (Eldenk et al., submitted 2026-05-11).
does_not_prove: Drift is within one speculation chain, not across K=0 gaps or catch-up.
bearing: C3': bears on how much stale/missing draft context matters

title: Test-Time Speculation
quote: acceptance lengths decrease consistently for all tasks and speculators
proves: Acceptance length of DFlash, EAGLE-3, PARD degrades with output length: MATH-500 Qwen3-8B from ~3.7 (first 10K tokens) to ~1.5 (last 10K); EAGLE-3 ~1.1 after ~20K; DFlash on Qwen3.6-35B 15 to 1.7 within ~25K tokens on AIME-2025.
does_not_prove: Not tied to K=0 catch-up or preemption; long-generation effect only.
bearing: C3'/C7': acceptance drifts with length, so equivalence checks must compare at matched positions

title: [Spec][Test] Add adaptive speculative decoding CI coverage (#31516)
quote: 24-way load forces retract, all finish, no leak/crash
proves: Closed unmerged 2026-09-20 by bot (author had too many idle PRs). Added TestAdaptiveRetract with tiny KV + SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT forcing retraction.
does_not_prove: Test checks finish/no leak/no crash, not exact output or acceptance equivalence.

title: Efficient Testing of Recovery Code Using Fault Injection
venue: ACM Transactions on Computer Systems 29(4), Article 11
quote: A critical part of developing a reliable software system is testing its recovery code.
proves: LFI library-level fault injection targeting recovery code; found 12 previously unreported bugs (MySQL, Git, BIND, Pidgin, PBFT); raised recovery-code coverage from ~0 to 60% automatically.
does_not_prove: General software; nothing on LLM serving.

quote: NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 8.0 or higher.
proves: Batch invariance requires NVIDIA CC >= 8.0 (also AMD gfx90a/gfx942/gfx950, Intel XPU with Triton).

title: PostgreSQL 18: 26.2. Log-Shipping Standby Servers
quote: the server might recycle old WAL segments before the standby has received them. If this occurs, the standby will need to be reinitialized from a new base backup.
proves: Without archiving, recycled WAL forces a standby rebuild from a base backup; wal_keep_size or a replication slot avoids it. Catch-up time grows with how long the standby was down.
does_not_prove: No sentence literally says the standby "can catch up provided it retains enough segments"; the page states the failure case and the retention fix.
bearing: C3' analogy: lazy catch-up needs the missing range retained, else full rebuild
